meta.purpose: Every deliberate departure from the legacy copy, in one auditable place. content-inventory.json is the verbatim harvest of what the old site said and is never edited; this file is what the rebuild says instead, and why.
meta.how_it_is_applied: ContentInventory reads the inventory, then applies this file on top. Nothing here is applied silently — ContentOverridesTest asserts that every `from` string is actually present in the inventory, so a correction whose target text changes upstream fails the build instead of quietly doing nothing.

decisions.question: The ten source typos catalogued in content-inventory.json meta.source_defects — fix or keep?
decisions.rationale: All are unambiguous errors and none change Simón's meaning. Two of them (PROYECTS, Porfolio) were already listed as defects 1 and 3 in plan §1.5.
decisions.consequence: The plan's §4.2 acceptance criterion — 'byte-identical to the legacy copy except the deliberate portfolio rewrite' — now reads 'except the departures enumerated in this file'.

decisions.question: menu_items.linkedin's Japanese label uses HALFWIDTH katakana (ﾘﾝｹﾄﾞｲﾝ) where every other Japanese string on the site is fullwidth, including social_links.linkedin (リンクトイン).
decisions.rationale: Simón's explicit call. Recorded here so a later session does not read it as an unnoticed bug and 'fix' it — the inconsistency between the menu label and the socials label is intentional and must survive.

decisions.question: social_links.rym and both documents carry a single untranslated <span> in the legacy markup — no en/ja variants exist at all.
decisions.rationale: RYM takes the full brand name in es/en and a katakana transliteration in ja, matching how Last.FM is already handled (Last.FM / ラスト.エフエム). CV labels name the document's language in the reader's language, so a Japanese visitor sees スペイン語 / 英語 rather than the Spanish endonyms.

decisions.question: The portfolio project's own entry claims the site is vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, which this rebuild makes false. Its repo_url points at the legacy repo and the schema has one repo_url field.
decisions.choice: repo_url → portfolio-client, live_url → the live site, technologies → the real new stack. The API repo is named in the description body.
decisions.rationale: The client repo is the one a visitor clicking through from a portfolio card wants to see first. live_url was never set even though the site has always been live.

decisions.question: Japanese inline font-size overrides in the legacy markup.
decisions.choice: Not seeded at all — they stay in the inventory's legacy_style fields and never enter the database.
decisions.rationale: They are presentation, not content. Plan §4.2 'Watch for'. Session 5 solves CJK sizing in CSS; §6 lists which strings carried them.

corrections_note: `where` is a dotted path into content-inventory.json. A list of objects is indexed by its `key` field, so `projects.ambient` selects the entry whose key is 'ambient'. The replacement applies to every string beneath the resolved node, which is what lets one entry fix a paragraph list (profile.about.es) or a {lead, items, trailing} block in one go. Only description_blocks is corrected, never description_legacy_html — that field is the reference copy of what the old markup said and is not seeded.

client_side_corrections.note: ui_strings are not database rows — they become i18n message keys in the client (content-inventory.json ui_strings.note). This correction therefore has to be applied by session 5 when the message catalogue is written, not by a seeder. Listed here so the decision is not lost between sessions.

The same typo as profile.meta_description.es, which IS corrected in the database. This is the client-side copy of the string; session 5 must fix it in the message catalogue too, or the two will disagree about the site's own description.

icons.reason: The harvest records Font Awesome classes (`fa-brands fa-github`). Session 5 deletes Font Awesome entirely — it costs ~100 KB plus webfonts and a blocking CDN origin for about a dozen glyphs (plan §1.5 defects 17 and 18) — and replaces it with @nuxt/icon, server-bundled so the SVGs inline and no CDN is touched. The icon name is content, so the mapping lands in the database now rather than as a lookup table in the client.
icons.sets: Brands come from @iconify-json/simple-icons and UI glyphs from @iconify-json/tabler, matching plan §4.5 step 3.
icons.unverified: These names have NOT been checked against the installed icon packages — neither package is installed until session 5. Session 5 must verify every one of them renders and correct any that do not. `rym` deliberately uses a tabler headphones glyph rather than a brand icon, mirroring the legacy markup, which also used a generic headphones glyph rather than a RateYourMusic logo.

portfolio.reason: Plan §4.2 step 6. Every locale's closing sentence claimed the site was built in vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript. This is the one place the migration is deliberately not verbatim.

es.lead: Portafolios personal estilizado, animado y multi-lenguaje. Necesitaba un portafolios, entonces lo hice.
items: Front-end en Nuxt 4, renderizado en el servidor y cacheado con ISR
API REST en Laravel 13 sobre PostgreSQL, con todo el contenido traducido en la base de datos
Tres idiomas —español, inglés y japonés— cada uno con su propia URL
Panel de administración para editar cada texto, imagen y proyecto sin tocar código
es.trailing: Hecho en dos repositorios: el cliente en Nuxt y la API en Laravel. Sin librería de componentes, los diálogos y menús son elementos nativos del navegador.

en.lead: Stylized, animated, and multi-lingual personal portfolio. I needed one, so I made it.
items: Nuxt 4 front end, server-rendered and cached with ISR
Laravel 13 REST API on PostgreSQL, with every piece of content translated in the database
Three languages —Spanish, English and Japanese— each on its own URL
An admin panel for editing every string, image and project without touching code
en.trailing: Built as two repositories: the Nuxt client and the Laravel API. No component library — the dialogs and menus are native browser elements.

ja.lead: スタイリッシュでアニメーション豊かな、マルチリンガルな個人ポートフォリオ。必要だったので、自分で作りました
items: Nuxt 4のフロントエンド。サーバーサイドレンダリングとISRによるキャッシュ
PostgreSQL上のLaravel 13のREST API。すべてのコンテンツをデータベースで多言語管理
スペイン語・英語・日本語の3言語、それぞれに専用のURL
コードを触らずにテキスト・画像・プロジェクトを編集できる管理パネル
ja.trailing: NuxtのクライアントとLaravelのAPI、2つのリポジトリで構築。コンポーネントライブラリは使わず、ダイアログやメニューはブラウザのネイティブ要素で実装しています。
